name: Lamb Cuts
summary: Rack, chops and leg to roast or grill, shoulder and shanks to braise.

sections.heading: The cuts
blocks: Lamb follows the same rule as beef: the loin and rib are tender and cooked quickly, often to medium-rare; the shoulder and legs' lower ends are tough and braised. Its fat carries most of the distinctive flavor; trim thick fat if you'd like it milder.

rows: Cut into elegant rib chops after resting. Medium-rare to medium.
Like tiny T-bones; a few minutes a side.
Roast at 325–375°F (160–190°C), or butterfly and grill
The classic roast; rub with garlic, rosemary and lemon.
Falls apart after a few hours; great for stews and curries.
One per person; braise 2–3 hours until the meat slides off the bone.
Cook to 160°F (71°C), like all ground meat.

blocks: Doneness temperatures for lamb are the same as beef: see the [doneness chart](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#doneness-chart).
